title: Finally got approved on Steam 😁 Let me know what you think!
author: qwertyasdfghzxcvbnui
selftext:
After 4 years of learning gamedev, I've finally used AI to help me complete a project and get it approved on Steam! 

18 wishlists in 24 hours 😁

Let me know what you guys think, happy to answer any questions dev-related. 

I'm obviously breaking some rules on releasing a game with so few wishlists, but I'm proud of what I made and think if it's good, people will play it and share it 🙏 we'll see!

[https://store.steampowered.com/app/4488180/Dark\_Fantasy\_Tower\_Defense/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/4488180/Dark_Fantasy_Tower_Defense/)

replies.author: qwertyasdfghzxcvbnui
replies.body:
Thank you 🙏

I can request for steam keys on the 24th and will be going back through everyone's comments and will be sure to get you a key! I would love the feedback.

For my dev process, it started out kinda awkward, uploading .gd scripts to chatgpt and having 10 page PDF outline that grew to 30 pages by the time i was done. I would feed that to the new conversations until i hit the max on the thread (i capped out about 40 threads). Back and forth, so much testing, but it worked. Just very very inefficient. Also, I have huge game bible documents and plans and outlines of all of my thoughts, i would give that to Chat and ask it to fill in any missing gaps  so i wouldn't have to redo work.

Codex + VS Code is what made the difference for me.

I previously had it setup for my UE5 game I've been working on for about 18 months, but i didn't have much luck in UE5 with it and preferred doing the work myself (maybe AI skill issue on my part). 

But Godot seemed to handle things a lot better. 

I didn't have a perfect process at the beginning, but stuck with it and day by day completed it. Evolved the process and really learned a ton about myself and my passion along the way.

replies.author: MoshPunk
replies.body:
It's pretty simple to setup. Get yourself VS Code and add the extension for Codex. If you prefer Claude Code, there's an extension for that in VS Code as well. VS Code has a tab to search for extensions. Think of VS Code as where you'll make all your scripts for Godot. You'll need to point VS Code to the main directory of your project. This should work with any engine you choose, but I'd recommend Godot and do a 2D game. 

Here's a screenshot of what VS Code looks like and the Extensions tab for reference:

https://preview.redd.it/sykj6m1s3vpg1.png?width=602&format=png&auto=webp&s=c05f5c09072450d84b93737a931dae34c18d0b67



Codex and Claude are great in VS Code because they can see all the files in the directory and make decisions based on your entire codebase. Context is key when using AI though. If you want AI to do something, you need to give it great detail for the task for it to be as close as possible. Any missing context can result in unwanted side-effects.   
  
This is where you want to use something called "Git." Git gives you version control so if something gets so out of whack, you can just go back to a previous working version. Git also has an extension for VS Code as is shown in the above screenshot.

And for the version history, i just copy paste it below and block-comment it and give it title version 1.2 and so on. Lol, i am newbs and primitive.
